title: Go: HTTP Client
description: Make HTTP requests from Go using the net/http client — GET, POST, timeouts, and custom headers.

steps.title: HTTP GET request
steps.description: Use `http.Get("https://httpbin.org/get")` to make a GET request. Print the status code using `resp.StatusCode` and `resp.Status`. Close the response body.

verification.failureMessage: Remember to close the response body with defer.

steps.title: Read response body
steps.description: Make a GET request to `https://httpbin.org/anything`. Read the entire response body using `io.ReadAll(resp.Body)` and print it as a string.
hints: The response body is a stream — read it before closing

verification.failureMessage: Use io.ReadAll to read the full body.

steps.title: HTTP POST with JSON
steps.description: Send a POST request to `https://httpbin.org/post` with a JSON body `{"name":"Go"}`. Set `Content-Type` to `application/json`. Print the status code and response body.
hints: Set Content-Type as the second argument to Post

verification.successMessage: POST with JSON body sent successfully!
verification.failureMessage: The body argument needs an io.Reader — use strings.NewReader.

steps.title: Client with timeout
steps.description: Create a custom `http.Client` with a 5-second timeout. Use it to make a GET to `https://httpbin.org/delay/2` (which takes 2 seconds). Print the status code.
hints: A 5s timeout handles the 2s delay successfully

verification.failureMessage: Set the Timeout field on the http.Client struct.

steps.title: Custom headers
steps.description: Create a GET request to `https://httpbin.org/headers` with a custom header `X-Custom: GoRules`. Use `http.NewRequest` and set the header with `req.Header.Set()`. Execute with a default client and print the response body.

verification.successMessage: Custom header sent and echoed back!
verification.failureMessage: Use http.NewRequest to create a request with custom headers.
